w1: In Maharashtra, more than one lakh co-operative housing societies are run by committees of unpaid volunteers.
w2: Those volunteers sign off on lakhs of rupees, and they are personally responsible for that money.
w3: Registrars dissolve committees that can't show a recorded resolution for their spending.
w4: Apps like MyGate record who approved a payment.
w4b: None of them check whether that person was allowed to approve it.
w5: We built Society Room to close that gap.
b1: Society Room makes sure money leaves a society only after three things are true.
b3: A meeting with enough members voted for it, and every vote is recorded by name.
b4: And the amount is within the limit the society's bye-laws allow.
b5: Honest committee members get protection, and residents get answers they can trust.
b6: The society's auditor gets a clean, tamper-proof record to sign off on.
s1: Switch is what puts our AI agents into the team chat.
s2: One Switch template creates two rooms: a private committee room, and a general-body room for residents.
s3: It also adds four agents: a Clerk, a Treasurer Agent, a Byelaw agent, and a Concierge.
s4: Switch decides who is allowed to give each agent instructions.
s5: If someone who isn't the treasurer agent's owner tells it to pay, Switch stops the message before the agent ever sees it.
s6: The money rules themselves are fixed code, not AI guesswork. The AI only reports the result.
d2: A resident tells the treasurer agent: just pay it. Switch blocks the message.
d3: Even the Treasurer is refused, because there's no resolution yet.
d4: So the Treasurer, chairing the meeting, opens one.
d5: The Clerk counts quorum: forty-one present, twenty needed.
d6: It records the vote by name, and the motion passes, four to one.
d7: The Byelaw agent confirms sixty-eight thousand rupees is within the one-lakh limit.
d8: Only now does the Treasurer Agent book the payment.
d10: That's over the bye-law limit, so even a committee vote can't approve it. It goes straight to the annual general meeting agenda.
d11: Finally, in the residents' room, a member asks why the society paid for the lift.
d12: The Concierge answers by quoting the published ledger and meeting minutes.
c1: Switch decides who may give instructions.
c1b: The code decides what is allowed.
c2: Society Room. Governance your auditor can sign.
